headline: Dolores Huerta died at 96. She coined "Sí, se puede."
summary: Dolores Huerta died at home on Wednesday at 96, her family said. She was a teacher in California's San Joaquin Valley who quit because her students came to class hungry. In 1962 she and César Chavez founded the union that became United Farm Workers. She was jailed 22 times and received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2012.

cover_question.q: Why did she go to jail 22 times?

cover_answer: For marching with farm workers. She kept going.
table_question: Would you keep a secret for 60 years to protect something you built?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: A woman named Dolores Huerta died on Wednesday. She was 96, as old as a great-great-grandmother. She spent her whole life helping the people who pick our fruit and vegetables get paid fairly, and her saying was "Sí, se puede," which means "Yes, it can be done." She lived a long, full life, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Only if it comes up. One long life, one saying they can repeat.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old takes one vivid feature for the event, so the script gives them a saying to repeat and the people who pick the fruit they eat, and leaves the rest out. This age fears what it can picture, so 96 is pinned to a great-great-grandmother, not their age or yours. Expect "are you going to die?" Not for a long time.

8-12.script: Dolores Huerta quit teaching because her students came to class hungry. In 1962 she and César Chavez started a union for the people picking the crops. A union is a whole class refusing to play until the rule is fair: one picker can be replaced, thousands can't. The grape strike they led ran five years.
8-12.why: Hungry students, a union, a five-year strike. The chain is her life.
8-12.why_long: This age follows cause and effect, so the script runs her life as a chain: hungry students, a union, a five-year strike. The class refusing to play is the mechanism, and it says why one picker alone could not have done it. Expect "did she win?" Yes, the first health plans for farm workers, after five years on strike.

13-17.script: Would you keep a secret for 60 years to protect your life's work? Dolores Huerta built the United Farm Workers with César Chavez. This year she said he sexually abused her, and that she kept quiet so the movement would not unravel. Second: does "Sí, se puede" survive the man beside her?
13-17.why: The work, and what it cost her. Let them say which weighs more.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: the union she built changed farm workers' lives, and the man she built it with abused her, a secret kept 60 years to protect it. The script asks whether the slogan survives it, where they test whether you argue honestly. Expect "was she right to stay quiet?" Her cross to bear, she said.

5-7.q: Why did she go to jail 22 times?
5-7.a: For marching and standing up for the farm workers. It wasn't for doing something bad. She kept going anyway.

8-12.a: Everyone stops work at once until the boss agrees a fair deal.
He gave her the Medal of Freedom and said he had stolen her slogan.

13-17.q: Why did she wait 60 years to tell?
13-17.a: She feared it would unravel what farm workers had won, she said.

13-17.q: Does this change what Chavez did?
13-17.a: The work stands and so does the harm. Say where you land.
